# Circular path-gradient native controls

Original manually assembled OOXML, generated by tools/path_gradient_fixture.py
from this project's original shape-theme package. No corpus artwork or text is
copied. The reference application produced native.pdf with tools/export-reference.ps1.
The initial twelve-control native page was visually inspected. The source passes both standard
and supported-extension schema views.

Twenty-four rectangular shapes cross six fillToRect settings (omitted, centered point,
top-right point, bottom-left point, central area, outside point) with opaque and
20%-alpha final stops and two/three stops. Three-stop fills use red/green/blue
at 0/50/100%; two-stop fills use red/blue at 0/100%.

ECMA-376 Part 1 sections 20.1.8.31 and 20.1.8.46 define the focal rectangle and
path shading. The reference application ignores the different focal rectangles in these circle
controls: each PDF radial shading is centered at (105,32.5) in its 210x65pt shape,
with radius 109.91pt, matching half the diagonal. This is a measured reference/spec
divergence, not a proposed generalization to rectangular or shape path modes.

record_path_gradient_reference.py extracts shading coordinates and color functions
straight from the reference application's PDF and binds source/PDF/case hashes. Opaque three-stop color
functions are linear. Alpha controls introduce intermediate color segments and
PDF transparency resources; color functions alone do not describe the final
composited pixels. The recorder also stores 216 composited native pixel samples at 288 DPI.

Browser regressions compare transparent pixels at matching 288 DPI and opaque
colors directly against native PDF color functions at each browser pixel center,
through insertion,
export, exact undo and reopening. Opaque colors use a three-channel-level tolerance; the five-channel-level
transparent tolerance accounts for
PDF radial-shading rasterization differences, which decrease with resolution.
The geometry is also checked directly against native PDF coordinates.

This fixture uses 210x65pt rectangular shapes with local coordinates. Broader
shape transforms retain the existing painting pipeline; the corpus memo exercises
grouped artwork. Rectangular/shape path modes and nonzero tile rectangles remain
unsupported.
